anomalies.observed: Both ground pins on each isolated CAN transceiver are connected to the same GND net.
anomalies.expected: The transceivers’ primary and bus-side grounds should remain separate for the specified CAN galvanic isolation.
anomalies.impact: The shared ground defeats galvanic isolation, allowing ground-loop and common-mode disturbances to pass between the CAN bus side and the board.

anomalies.observed: The two 120-ohm resistors connect /CAN0_N to SW6.1 and /CAN1_N to SW6.2; the other switch pair connects /CAN1_P to SW6.3 and /CAN0_P to SW6.4. Closing the corresponding DIP switches therefore couples the two CAN buses rather than terminating each bus across its own P/N pair.
anomalies.expected: If these are termination switches, each should connect a 120-ohm resistor across the P and N lines of its own CAN bus, while keeping CAN0 and CAN1 separate.
anomalies.impact: With the switches closed, the CAN interfaces are coupled together and are not independently terminated; this can cause bus loading, communication errors, or unintended interaction between the two networks.

parsed.summary: The design files connect both sides of each isolated CAN transceiver to common ground, defeating the specified galvanic isolation. The CAN switch and 120-ohm resistor wiring also appears to couple the two CAN buses instead of providing per-bus termination.
